details.detail: Surface detail: value, panel tone, seams, fastener rows, slat band, gear stripe, placards, grime
details.note: Near-far value FIXED: w19A near flap (600,440) 162 -> 173, (560,500) 164 -> 175; far outboard skin x=580-640 y 130-160 141-164 -> 113-139 (ratio ~0.70, KN41 194 -> 146 = 0.75). No banding from the steeper ramp. Fastener rows now give fine detail, but read as stitching: double/triple columns of 1-px dots at 98-162 on a 169 flap (0.58; KN41 single soft rows 136 on 170 = 0.80), riding on a strip that is 5-12 L LIGHTER than the skin (w19A row 520: strip 174-176 vs flap 169; w26K rows 280-290: 184-188 vs 175), so at range the rows become pale ladders. Hinge smudges are flat hard-edged rectangles (w19A 149-153 on 164-170, 5-7 px tall, 20-30 px long) = tape, not soot.

Pod bodies unchanged (w26K x=600 flank 120 -> 65, identical to r16); the near-pod top now carries a lit crown band (w26K x=560 y 308-312: 131/136 -> 173/185), closer to _7250's white-topped prism. Far pods unchanged.

Bulb gone: now a low blister on the fan cowl, a saddle, then the rise to the strut, nose just aft of the inlet split (x_pylon_high, x_pylon_side) - the _137 sequence. Residuals: the crown outline is faceted (straight runs and kinks from the 8-segment loft, visible in x_pylon_side / c_nacelle_left as a lumpy top), the tent-tapered flank meets the cowl along a hard shading step, and from w13A the blister is lower and flatter than _137's dome (reads as a skirted cap).

w11A row 420 throat 13-37 -> 16-37 (lip end slightly lighter, LALF _136 31-66). But w11K row 450 now 82 -> 59 vs r16 81 -> 50: the fan end got LIGHTER, opposite to the intent (knav _9 falls to ~10). Spinner still unreadable from seats.
FIXED: the 14-pin dark comb in w19A is now 7 fine light wicks (no fringe); n19A glow sits flush in the tip instead of a cherry on top.

New: rivet strips lighter than the skin (pale bands/ladders in w26K and on the outboard skin in w19A), smudges as tape, and visible 1-px dot crawl on the near rows; pylon crown faceting. No z-fighting, gaps or floating parts.
